title: A balanced meal on a budget
outcome: FOODWISE: plan a balanced meal on a budget.
goal: I can plan one balanced meal, check its cost and explain my choices.
success: I can name the food groups in my meal.
I can add the ingredient costs and stay within £2.00.
I can choose a safe three-step dish for next week and give a reason.
model_dish: Cold bean and vegetable wrap with fruit and plain yoghurt
model_reason: My £1.40 meal has starchy food from the wrap, protein from beans, vegetables and fruit, and dairy from yoghurt. It leaves 60p of my £2.00 budget.
price_basis: All prices are invented for this lesson. Each price covers the stated amount for one person. These are ingredient-use costs, not the cost of buying whole packs. No spending or shopping is required. Water is available at no charge in this classroom model.
plate: Aim for plenty and a variety over the day.
Choose wholegrain or higher-fibre options when suitable.
Beans, lentils, eggs, fish or meat are examples.
Choose an unsweetened, calcium-fortified alternative where needed.
Use unsaturated types in small amounts when used.
No added oil is needed for this cold dish
plate_note: The two largest groups in a balanced eating pattern are vegetables and fruit, and starchy foods. Include protein foods and dairy or suitable alternatives. Use small amounts of oils and spreads. Balance is built across the day or week; every meal does not need exact plate sections. Choose water as a drink. No calorie counting, weight talk or food judgement is needed.
recipe: With adult approval, wash the vegetables and fruit. Grate the carrot and finely slice the cabbage using the agreed tools. An adult can prepare these for you.
Use 80 g of ready-to-eat cooked beans, drained by an adult if needed. Mash with a fork. Mix in about 20 g of the plain yoghurt and the vegetables.
Put the filling on the wrap. Fold it. Serve with the washed fruit and the rest of the yoghurt. Keep it chilled until eaten and follow the adult’s plan.
safety: Tell the adult about dietary and access needs privately. The adult checks every ingredient label and the agreed allergy plan before ingredients are issued.
Wash hands with soap and water before food preparation, after the toilet and after touching waste. Dry them well. Tie hair back, cover cuts and clean the work surface and tools.
Use knives, graters and open tins only with adult approval and supervision. Keep fingers away from sharp edges. Ask for pre-cut vegetables or adult help.
Use beans labelled cooked and ready to eat. Dry beans need a different cooking process and are not used here. Keep ready-to-eat food away from raw food.
Keep chilled ingredients at 5°C or below, follow use-by dates and storage labels, and take out only what you need. The adult handles storage and any leftovers.
Tasting is optional. Never share a tasting spoon. If anything spills, breaks or feels unsafe, stop, put the tool down and tell the adult. Clear and clean using the agreed routine.
allergy: The model contains wheat including gluten and milk. Soya is present in the optional alternative. All ingredients and alternatives need label checks for all relevant allergens and cross-contact. A plant alternative is not automatically suitable. If a safe substitution is unavailable, use the planning or simulation route. Never describe a meal as allergen-free.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: The design brief
pupil: Plan one meal for one person.
Your ingredient-use budget is £2.00.
Today is planning. We will prepare the agreed dish next week.
stages.teacher: Read the brief aloud. Ask what the meal must do: offer variety, cost no more than £2.00 and be possible in a short supervised practical. Explain that the prices are invented and no one needs to discuss home spending. Offer spoken planning or a private adult check. Use the last minute as a quiet settling reset.
stages.check: Ask: Whose meal and what limit? Expect one person and £2.00. Re-read the brief if either is missing.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: A balanced eating pattern
pupil: Name a food group for a wrap, beans and carrot.
Which groups could fruit and yoghurt add?
Balance builds over the day or week.
stages.teacher: Use the balanced plate recap. Invite food group sorting, with the model meal as an example rather than a rule for every meal. Explain that protein is a nutrient in several foods; beans are counted in the protein group for this model to avoid double counting. Oils are used in small amounts when needed, not added to tick a box.
stages.check: Wrap is starchy food; beans supply protein; carrot is a vegetable. Fruit adds variety and yoghurt adds dairy. Read the recap again if pupils use only colour as a test of balance.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: A model meal and its cost
pupil: Watch the six ingredient costs being added.
Check the total and money left.
See the three steps for next week.
stages.teacher: Point to each amount and price. Add 35p + 30p + 15p + 10p + 20p + 30p = 140p, or £1.40. Then £2.00 minus £1.40 = £0.60. Name the food groups and model the one-line reason. Explain the three recipe steps using empty-hand gestures only. No food or sharp tools are needed today. Fade the model by asking pupils to supply the final addition.
stages.check: Ask: Is 140p £1.40 or £14.00? Expect £1.40. Show 100p plus 40p and repeat the check if needed.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: A change within the budget
pupil: Replace the 30p apple with a 35p pear.
Find the new total and money left.
Explain what stays balanced.
stages.teacher: Calculate the change together: £1.40 minus £0.30 plus £0.35 = £1.45. The budget left is 55p. Record why fruit is still present. Read the price basis and distinguish a portion cost from a full pack price. Ask a pupil to explain the method to a partner or adult. Keep household finances private.
stages.check: Accept £1.45 and 55p. If the old item is still charged, cross it out, subtract it and add the replacement once.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: The cost check
pupil: A plan costs £1.40. It has £2.00 to spend.
Choose the amount left: 60p, £1.40 or £3.40.
Explain one safe preparation rule.
stages.teacher: Use the hinge choices. Correct answer is 60p because 200p minus 140p equals 60p. If any learner chooses another answer, rehearse with written pence amounts before independent work. Parallel check: a £1.55 meal leaves 45p. Also ask why ready-to-eat beans matter and why a grater needs approval. No tasting or preparation takes place today.
stages.check: Move on when pupils can show subtraction or explain the budget comparison. If not, use the Supported route with paired checking and keep the independent evidence pupil-owned.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: My meal plan
pupil: In your book, plan your dish and list quantities.
Add the prices and find the money left.
Write one reason it is balanced.
Choose the three-step wrap method for next week, or an adult-approved adaptation.
stages.teacher: Use the meal plan prompts and one route. Pupils may use the model ingredients but make and explain their own choice. An adult can scribe the pupil’s words and read them back. Check food groups, arithmetic and a feasible dish. A different dish needs a checked two- or three-step method, suitable ingredients and adult approval before practical use. Use the last minute to pause, review the list and organise the book.
stages.check: The core evidence is an ingredient list with quantities, total at or below £2.00 and a one-line balanced-meal reason. Note an unfinished plan honestly. Record support used.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: A plan ready to use
pupil: Check a total against the budget.
Check the food groups and one-line reason.
Read the safety card and keep one change.
stages.teacher: Offer a partner check by consent or an adult check. The pupil makes one correction if needed. The adult marks next-week readiness as approved or pending after checking method, ingredients, dietary needs and equipment. Keep tasting optional. Use the final minute for a calm tidy reset. Do not label an unmade dish as completed.
stages.check: Use the evidence sheet. A balanced meal within budget meets the planning task; practical approval is a separate safety gate.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My design choice
pupil: My meal costs ___ and leaves ___.
It is balanced because ___.
Next week I will prepare ___, subject to the adult check.
stages.teacher: Ask each pupil for their own cost and reason, privately if preferred. Retain the plan in the book and record the page. Keep any unresolved dietary or equipment checks pending. Week 2 uses the agreed plan. This week provides planning evidence only.
stages.check: Accept exact confirmed scribing, oral explanation linked to the plan, or independent writing. Keep actual evidence separate from the adult model.

Supported: Use the model wrap and choose apple or pear.
Read or hear each price. Tick off each item once in your book.
Add in pence with an adult or calculator, then check against 200p.
Say your own reason using: My meal has ___ from ___ and costs ___.
Standard: Choose the model meal or swap ingredients from the card.
List the exact amounts and add their prices. Work out the money left.
Explain how your choices include the main food groups.
Keep the three-step method and identify two safety actions for next week.
Stretch: Complete the core plan and one-line reason first.
Cost a second version using two substitutions. Keep it within £2.00.
Compare cost, food groups, likely texture and practical demands.
Justify which version you would prepare. Include a limitation of invented portion prices.

vocabulary: A variety of foods that helps meet our needs over time.
A food used in a dish.
Actions that keep food and equipment clean and safe.
When an allergen gets into another food by contact.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one step at a time. Read the price card aloud. Model an addition, then leave the next one for the pupil. Use pence throughout before converting to pounds. Offer a calculator and a repeated checklist.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing or pupil-directed scribing. Give thinking time and a brief choice before an open question. Read the final plan back so the pupil can correct it.
adaptations.SEMH: Use invented prices and a fictional design brief. No home spending, body, weight or personal diet disclosures. Avoid good-food or bad-food labels. Offer a private adult review and a calm pause with an agreed return.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: No food handling or tasting is required today. Provide a clear large-print view. Offer pre-prepared vegetables and adult tool handling for the later practical. Plan a suitable route before any food is issued.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pair ingredient names with the price row and food group. Read quantities and money aloud. Use the pupil’s own words with confirmed translation or scribing where available.

misconceptions: A balanced dish needs equal food group sections.
Balance is built across the day or week. Groups have different proportions and oils are used in small amounts.
A portion price is the price of a full pack.
This card charges only for the stated amount used. Buying whole packs may cost more.
Changing an ingredient means adding a second full cost.
Remove the old cost before adding the new one.
Any beans can go straight into a cold wrap.
Only cooked beans labelled ready to eat are used here. Dry beans require a separate cooking process.
careers: Food designers and catering teams balance cost, nutrition, access and safe preparation. A clear plan helps another person prepare the intended meal.
fallback: Without food, equipment, printer or paper, read the price rows aloud. Pupils speak, sign or direct their ingredient choices. Rehearse the three steps with empty hands. An adult records exact choices, total and reason when a recording method is available. Mark transcription pending until it exists. This is planning or simulation, never a claim that the meal was prepared.
